source.title: Variational Stochastic Gradient Descent for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Anna Kuzina; Hao-Tian Chen; Babak Esmaeili; J. Tomczak

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer families on image-classification test performance using a different optimizer and evaluation setup from the version’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy comparisons among VSGD, Adam, AdamW, and momentum SGD. The V4 rows below retain the Adam/AdamW and SGD results; VSGD results are not mapped to V4 because VSGD is the new method under evaluation, not one of the adaptive methods named in the version. Cited optimizer findings are not treated as this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study's Adam, AdamW and momentum-SGD comparisons directly measure V4's held-out-performance contrast on image classifiers. Its tuning includes weight decay and SGD momentum, so it does not reproduce V4's learning-rate-and-schedule-only condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they present VSGD as outperforming baseline optimizers with competitive convergence on image classification. Their conclusion claims consistent outperformance, although Table 1 contains exceptions, particularly TinyImageNet/ResNeXt-18. They do not establish a general adaptive-versus-SGD ordering.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a newly proposed probabilistic optimizer with Adam, AdamW, and momentum SGD on image classification. It reports grid searches over learning rate, weight decay for AdamW/VSGD, and momentum for SGD, then selects using validation data; this does not match the specific limited-tuning protocol in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The optimizer comparison varies across dataset and architecture. The paper also reports that VSGD accuracy changes with γ on CIFAR100/ConvMixer (Section C, Table 6), but that sensitivity result does not test a listed claim version.
record.problems: The comparison uses only two image-classification datasets for the main optimizer results and three random seeds. Table 1 reports averaged accuracies without per-seed values or error bars. Hyperparameter selection uses validation data, and the paper does not test the particular limited-tuning setup or language benchmarks in V4.
record.rows_left_out: VSGD and its weight-decay variants are omitted from V4 rows because they are the proposed optimizer rather than the adaptive methods named in that version. ImageNet reports VSGD 72.7% and Adam 69.8%, but has no momentum-SGD comparator, so it does not test V4’s adaptive-versus-SGD contrast.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; a controlled comparison of narrow versus broader tuning; switching Adam to SGD; a controlled isolation of decoupled weight decay. Training losses are reported, but training accuracy is not.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Final training losses contextualize the held-out differences. For CIFAR100 VGG16/ConvMixer/ResNeXt-18, Adam losses are 0.0284/0.0094/0.0081, AdamW 0.0157/0.0094/0.0088, and SGD 0.0018/0.0027/0.0151. For TinyImageNet VGG19/ConvMixer/ResNeXt-18, Adam losses are 0.1900/0.8513/1.2680, AdamW 1.4722/0.6882/1.4089, and SGD 0.1954/0.7581/1.8158. In particular, TinyImageNet VGG19 Adam has slightly lower training loss but substantially worse test accuracy than SGD. This conclusion uses the text because no row captures training loss.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted Table 1 accuracies match the supplied text. The study is not an original source. Reversals under its broader tuning qualify scope rather than directly challenge V4's restricted-tuning statement. AdamW comparisons alone do not isolate a causal benefit of decoupled weight decay. Table 1 reports three-seed averages without error bars; the setup's wording about validation-based selection is ambiguous about selection across seeds. Proposed-method and ImageNet results were explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Language benchmarks; comparisons under the specific limited-tuning recipe in the version; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; broad tuning; whether training performance is equal or better in the compared settings.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: CIFAR100/VGG16 and TinyImageNet-200/VGG19, under the study's broader tuning
relationships.reason: R1–R3 and R10–R12 show Adam and AdamW below SGD: 66.8/66.6 versus 67.9, and 47.6/49.0 versus 50.9. This supports the performance contrast without establishing the restricted-tuning condition.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracies favor SGD over Adam and AdamW on both benchmarks, but the comparisons remain unverified and do not establish restricted tuning.

relationships.reason: R7 and R13 show only small SGD advantages, 0.3 and 0.5 percentage points; uncertainty in these differences is not quantified.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly trailed SGD slightly, but these comparisons remain unverified and uncertainty was unquantified.

relationships.reason: R4–R6 show Adam and AdamW exceeding SGD, 66.5 and 67.0 versus 65.4; the adaptive disadvantage does not extend to this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R8 shows AdamW exceeding SGD, 69.7 versus 68.5, whereas Adam is slightly worse in R7; the outcome depends on the adaptive optimizer.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD while Adam trailed slightly, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R14 shows no adaptive disadvantage: AdamW and SGD both reach 52.4, whereas Adam reaches 51.9 in R13.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly tied SGD while Adam scored lower, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R16–R18 show Adam and AdamW exceeding SGD, 48.8 and 48.9 versus 47.0; this qualifies extension of the disadvantage beyond restricted tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD under broader tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: CIFAR100 VGG16 and TinyImagenet-200 VGG19; Adam and AdamW compared with momentum SGD
reader_labels.reason: Adaptive optimizer accuracy is lower than momentum SGD in these settings (R1–R3, R10–R12). The paper’s hyperparameter search includes learning rate and weight decay, so this is not a direct test of the version’s limited-tuning condition.
